facts.fact: tech.africa reports EG-IX, Egypt's main internet exchange, is operating in Cairo (Telecom Egypt's Regional Data Hub at Smart Village, run on AMS-IX's IX-as-a-Service platform) with 18 member networks and 31 ports.

Traffic: 722.19 Gb/s (peak over the preceding day) at EG-IX on 2026-09-07, with 528.80 Gb/s flowing at the time and average traffic of about 443 Gb/s in each direction, per the exchange's live counter as cited by tech.africa.
Traffic: 875 Gb/s (peak across the year) at EG-IX in 2026, a figure AMS-IX gave informally and which tech.africa says has not appeared in a formal company statement; no exact date is given.

Global content, CDN and cloud networks are members at EG-IX: Meta (AS32934), Amazon (AS16509), Microsoft (AS8075), CDN77/DataPacket, ACE CDN, Medianova, Zenlayer, G-Core Labs, Kaopu Cloud and Huawei Cloud, per bgp.tools data cited by tech.africa.
Two Jordanian carriers, Jordan Telecommunications (AS8697) and Al Bahrainia al Urdunia Liltaknia (AS9038), are members at EG-IX in Cairo, alongside global content networks and ICANN's L-root.

systems.tiers: 5 Egyptian members (Telecom Egypt, TE Data, Vodafone Egypt, Etisalat Egypt, Link Egypt), 2 Jordanian carriers, a root server, 10 global content/CDN/cloud networks

note: Document also says AMS-IX put peak traffic at 250 to 875 Gb/s in under two years, but gives no dates and under two years, so no growing fact.
